\(\text{This is of type-II Clairaut's type $z =px+qx+f(p,q)$}\) 1

To find the singular integral
\(\dfrac{\partial z}{\partial a}=0\implies x=-\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+1}}--------(3)\),

\(\left(3\right)^2 + \left(4\right)^2 \Rightarrow x^2+y^2=\dfrac{a^2}{a^2+b^2+1}+\dfrac{b^2}{a^2+b^2+1}=\dfrac{a^2+b^2}{a^2+b^2+1} \)

Subracting from 1 both sides, we get,

\(1-x^2-y^2=\dfrac{1}{a^2+b^2+1}\)

\(\Rightarrow 1+a^2+b^2 = \dfrac{1}{1-x^2-y^2}\)

\(\therefore \quad \sqrt{1+a^2+b^2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2-y^2}}\dots(5)\)

and from (4),

\(x^2+y^2+z^2 =1 \qquad \text{ which is the singular solution.}\)
